Estimate five-day tail losses, market beta exposure, and an illustrative delta-based option hedge.

## Scope

Results describe the supplied historical snapshot or a stated simulation. Model fit and scenario estimates are not evidence of performance on new observations. See the project README for the execution record and limitations.

```{r}
source("R/analytics_support.R")
set.seed(42)
```

```{r}
# Tickers for the seven ETFs in our portfolio (same order used for the weights)
tickers <- c("VTI", "VEA", "VWO", "BND", "VNQ", "GLD", "QQQ")

# Portfolio weight on each ticker, in the same order as the tickers vector
weights <- c(0.35, 0.15, 0.10, 0.15, 0.10, 0.05, 0.10)

# Notional value of the position, in dollars
notional <- 100e6

# Safety check that the weights sum to one
stopifnot(abs(sum(weights) - 1) < 1e-8)
```

```{r}
# Training sample start and end dates
d1 <- "2020-01-01"
d2 <- "2024-12-31"

# Loop over the tickers and pull daily discrete returns for each one
# The first ticker seeds the object and later tickers merge in by date
for (i in 1:length(tickers)) {
  tmp <- market_returns(tickers[i], d1, d2, discrete = TRUE)
  if (i == 1) {
    ret_disc <- tmp
  } else {
    ret_disc <- merge(ret_disc, tmp, join = "inner")
  }
}
colnames(ret_disc) <- tickers

# Pull SPY discrete returns and merge on the same trading days
spy_disc <- market_returns("SPY", d1, d2, discrete = TRUE)
all_ret <- merge(ret_disc, spy_disc, join = "inner")
colnames(all_ret) <- c(tickers, "SPY")

# Split back into the asset block and the SPY column
asset_disc <- as.matrix(all_ret[, tickers])
spy_disc_v <- as.vector(all_ret[, "SPY"])

# Daily log returns for each asset and for SPY
asset_log <- log(1 + asset_disc)
spy_log <- log(1 + spy_disc_v)

# Daily portfolio log return using the analysis utility
# discrete = FALSE tells the helper to return log returns
port_log <- as.vector(weighted_returns(asset_disc, weights, discrete = FALSE))

# Quick check on the sample size
length(port_log)
```

```{r}
# Seed so the bootstrap is reproducible
set.seed(16)

# Bootstrap settings: number of draws and horizon in days
B <- 100000
horizon <- 5
n_obs <- length(port_log)

# Sample day indices with replacement, arranged as B rows of 5 days each
# Saving idx lets us reuse the identical draws for SPY in section 3
idx <- matrix(sample(1:n_obs, B * horizon, replace = TRUE), nrow = B)

# 5-day portfolio log return for each draw is the sum across the 5 sampled days
r5_port <- rowSums(matrix(port_log[idx], nrow = B))

# Convert each 5-day log return into a dollar P&L on the notional
pnl_port <- notional * (exp(r5_port) - 1)

# 5-day 99% VaR and ES in dollars using the analysis utility
var_es <- lower_tail_summary(pnl_port, 0.99)
var_es

# Store the ES (a negative dollar number) and its positive loss version
ES0 <- as.numeric(var_es["ES"])
ES0_loss <- -ES0
ES0_loss
```

```{r}
# Beta for each asset from a regression of asset log returns on SPY log returns
betas <- rep(NA, length(tickers))
for (i in 1:length(tickers)) {
  fit <- lm(asset_log[, i] ~ spy_log)
  betas[i] <- coef(fit)[2]
}

# Portfolio beta as the weighted sum of individual betas
beta_port <- sum(weights * betas)
beta_port

# Sanity check: regress the portfolio return on SPY directly
beta_check <- coef(lm(port_log ~ spy_log))[2]
beta_check

# Decomposition table: weight, beta, beta contribution, and dollar exposure
decomp <- data.frame(
  ticker = tickers,
  weight = weights,
  beta = round(betas, 3),
  beta_contribution = round(weights * betas, 3),
  dollar_exposure = scales::dollar(round(weights * betas * notional, 0))
)
decomp

# Total SPY-equivalent dollar exposure of the portfolio
spy_equiv_exposure <- beta_port * notional
scales::dollar(round(spy_equiv_exposure, 0))
```

```{r}
# SPY price at the end of the training sample, taken from the adjusted close
spy_px <- read_market_history("SPY",  from = "2024-12-01", to = "2025-01-01")[, 6]
S0 <- as.numeric(last(spy_px))
S0

# Put contract assumptions: ATM delta and contract multiplier
delta_put <- -0.5
mult <- 100

# 5-day SPY log returns using the SAME bootstrap indices as section 1
r5_spy <- rowSums(matrix(spy_log[idx], nrow = B))

# 5-day SPY discrete return for each draw, needed for the price change
spy_ret5 <- exp(r5_spy) - 1

# P&L of one put contract on each draw under the delta approximation
# delta is negative, so the contract gains when SPY falls
pnl_one_put <- delta_put * mult * S0 * spy_ret5

# Function that returns the hedged 99% ES for a given number of contracts
hedged_ES <- function(Nc) {
  pnl_hedged <- pnl_port + Nc * pnl_one_put
  as.numeric(lower_tail_summary(pnl_hedged, 0.99)["ES"])
}

# Target ES: shrink the unhedged ES magnitude by 7.5%
target_ES <- 0.925 * ES0

# Upper bound for the search: the number of contracts that would short a SPY
# notional equal to the portfolio's full SPY-equivalent exposure from section 2.
# A 7.5% ES cut needs far fewer than this, so it safely brackets the root.
Nc_max <- spy_equiv_exposure / (abs(delta_put) * mult * S0)

# Solve for the contract count where hedged ES hits the target
root <- uniroot(function(Nc) hedged_ES(Nc) - target_ES, interval = c(0, Nc_max))
Nc_exact <- root$root
Nc_exact
# Minimum whole number of contracts
Nc <- ceiling(Nc_exact)
Nc

# Verify the reduction with the whole number of contracts
ES_hedged <- hedged_ES(Nc)
c(unhedged = ES0, target = target_ES, hedged = ES_hedged)

# Actual percent reduction achieved
pct_cut <- (ES_hedged - ES0) / abs(ES0)
pct_cut

# Hedge notional and share of the SPY-equivalent exposure covered
hedge_notional <- Nc * mult * abs(delta_put) * S0
frac_hedged <- hedge_notional / spy_equiv_exposure
c(hedge_notional = hedge_notional, frac_of_exposure = frac_hedged)
```

## Interpretation limits

The hedge uses a constant option delta and excludes premium, gamma, implied volatility changes, expiry effects, and transaction costs. It is an illustrative scenario rather than an executable options strategy.
